title: Geometry-Resolved Projection of RF Imbalance to Ion Micromotion in a Same-Phase Dual-RF Blade Trap
authors: Chun-Yang Luan, Haiyu Ding, Cheng-Kang Pan, Xiangjie Li, Lin Cheng, Gangxi Wang, Yuting Lei, Peilin Zheng, Shixin Hu, Xiang Zhang, Fei Wang
abstract: Common-mode metrics of a high-$Q$ helical resonator do not determine the residual ion-side field in a dual-electrode drive. We combine a two-node differential RF model with single-electrode finite-element bases to obtain a computation-only, geometry-resolved projection for a same-phase blade trap. For a 3.5 pF external load per branch, the model gives a total effective branch capacitance of 7.640 pF and an HWHM-equivalent full branch-difference scale of 12.7 fF at $Q_{\mathrm{loaded}}=600$. The seven-segment geometry gives center and axial-RMS differential field coefficients of 640 V m$^{-1}$ and 635 V m$^{-1}$ per differential peak volt. A representative 10 fF mismatch with an effective 0.1 pF balance scale projects to 44.5/44.1 nm center/RMS $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ micromotion at 100 V common peak voltage. Supplementary thermal, bypass-admittance, and tested numerical cases characterize model sensitivity. All reported displacements are projections; no RF-bench or ion-side validation is claimed.
summary: This paper develops a sophisticated model to calculate the residual micromotion experienced by trapped ions due to imperfections in the trap's RF driving fields. By combining circuit theory with finite-element simulations, the authors provide a geometry-resolved projection that quantifies how small capacitance mismatches translate into measurable ion motion. This is vital for achieving high-precision quantum operations in trapped-ion quantum computing architectures.
main_problem: The study addresses how residual RF field imbalances, which are not captured by common-mode metrics, project onto measurable micromotion of trapped ions in a dual-RF blade trap.
main_result: The authors successfully developed a geometry-resolved projection method showing that even small capacitance mismatches (fF scale) can lead to tens of nanometers of projected ion micromotion.
method: The methodology combines a two-node differential RF circuit model with single-electrode finite-element simulations to factorize the error source into geometric and electrical components.
model_or_system: The physical system is a trapped ion setup utilizing a same-phase dual-RF blade trap geometry. The analysis models the coupling between the RF driving fields, electrode capacitances, and the resulting force on the trapped ion.
key_observables: Projected micromotion amplitude (nm), differential field coefficients ($	ext{V m}^{-1}$ per $V_d$), and effective differential capacitance scale ($C_{	ext{diff,bal}}$).
important_parameters: Capacitance mismatch ($\Delta C$, e.g., 10 fF), loaded quality factor ($Q_{\mathrm{loaded}}=600$), and common peak voltage (e.g., 100 V).
main_assumptions: All reported displacements are projections based on the model; no direct RF-bench or ion-side validation is claimed.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the factorization of the RF-to-ion mapping ($	ext{Eres} = \alpha_{	ext{diff}} H_{	ext{diff}} V_c$) and quantify how a specific capacitance mismatch translates into measurable micromotion, comparing balanced vs. unbalanced scenarios.
paper_structure: The paper establishes that common metrics are insufficient, develops the combined circuit/geometry model to factorize the error source, calculates key coefficients ($\alpha_{	ext{diff}}, H_{	ext{diff}}$), and then applies this framework to quantify micromotion for representative mismatch values. Supplementary sections analyze thermal and DC bypass sensitivities.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical tool for experimentalists working with trapped ions, moving beyond simple resonator characterization to predict systematic errors arising from electrode geometry and RF imbalance.
